source:
A comparison was made by us of the time taken to identify a misplaced label under two shelf arrangements. Arrangement A placed labels at the front edge; arrangement B placed them above the relevant shelf. Twelve participants performed one search under each arrangement, with the order alternated between participants.

The median search time in arrangement A was 19 seconds, whereas a median of 24 seconds was recorded in arrangement B. A broad conclusion of superiority would, however, exceed the evidential reach of this activity. No uncertainty interval was calculated, and the sample consisted of staff who already knew the room.

The task involved a single deliberately misplaced label. Ordinary searching may involve several labels, unfamiliar categories, or interruptions. It is thus the practical suggestion of a further trial that is supported by the results. A trial involving visitors would help determine whether the observed time difference also appears among people without prior familiarity with the shelves.
